title: Returned-Payment Fees Joining Plan Arrears on Benefit Overpayment Accounts — Ledger Guide
content:
Returned-payment fees join the arrears payment on a defaulted Benefit Overpayment Accounts repayment plan when plan installments came back unpaid. The fees that join are added to the arrears payment on top of its installment part.

## Which return entries are looked at

The return entries looked at are those among the entries taken for the installment credit: entries booked within the whole months elapsed from the plan's first installment due date to the handling date plus the month in progress, an entry being taken when the whole months from its booking date to the handling date are fewer than that number.

## Which fees join

| Repayments returned among those entries | Fees that join the arrears |
|---|---|
| Two or more | Every returned-payment fee standing unpaid on the overpayment |
| Exactly one | The most recent returned-payment fee |
| None | No fee |

Returned-payment fees stand unpaid to the extent the fees booked on the overpayment exceed the repayments applied to its fee component. The most recent returned-payment fee is the amount of the fee entry with the latest booking date on the overpayment's ledger.

## Reading the ledger (hypothetical entries)

The overpayment's ledger shows fee entries of USD 25.00, USD 30.00 and USD 40.00, booked in that order, and USD 25.00 of repayments applied to the fee component.

- Fees standing unpaid: USD 95.00 booked, less USD 25.00 applied, is USD 70.00.
- With two returns among the entries taken for the installment credit, USD 70.00 joins.
- With exactly one return among them, the most recent fee, USD 40.00, joins.
- With none among them, nothing joins, even though fees stand unpaid on the overpayment.
